reason: E3 directly supports that B addition refines the BCC phase and enhances passive film stability and wear resistance, partially supporting several premises. However, no cited evidence supports the specific Mo level (~0.25 molar), the rapid self-repair mechanism, or the direct link between microstructural refinement and reduced defect sites for pitting/mechanical damage. E2 and E4 only provide general context about HEAs in corrosive environments without addressing the specific mechanistic claims.
premises: Optimal alloying (e.g., ~0.25 Mo or B) refines the microstructure of HEAs.
A refined microstructure reduces defect sites (grain boundaries, interphases) that initiate pitting and mechanical damage.
Optimal alloying promotes formation of a uniform, adherent, defect-tolerant passive oxide film.
The refined microstructure and alloying enable rapid self-repair of the passive film after mechanical disruption.
This synergy minimizes total mass loss from combined wear and corrosion.
